solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Strut for instance extended across wood (6)

indicatorNotes.extended across: a word stretched out so it reaches across another ends up holding that word inside it

blocks.note: say = for instance, as in 'take, say, London'

annotation.surface: A plank of wood is laid across a gap to serve as a structural strut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strut' looks like a building support in this carpentry scene; it is the verb, to walk showily.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words describe a swaggering, showy walk.

entries.clue: Political diplomacy in newspaper, paramilitary offensive originally covered by broadcaster (4,5)

indicatorNotes.in: the newspaper is placed in the broadcaster, alongside the next piece
indicatorNotes.originally: the words are reduced to how they originally begin, their first letters
indicatorNotes.covered by: the broadcaster is laid over the other pieces like a cover, so they end up inside it

blocks.note: a sower broadcasts seed by scattering it

annotation.surface: A news report on a paramilitary attack, seen through a TV broadcaster's coverage.
annotation.walkthrough: The broadcaster is not a TV station but a farmer scattering seed by hand, the older sense of broadcast.
annotation.definitionFit: A political term: soft power means winning influence by persuasion and attraction rather than force, which is diplomacy's work.

entries.clue: Wobbly thing lets in winter air (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Wobbly: something wobbly will not hold steady, so its letters shift out of order

annotation.surface: A draughty, rickety window or door is letting the cold winter air in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winter air' reads as a cold draught; an air is also a tune, and this one is a Christmas carol.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the carol is a tune sung at Christmas, and air is the old word for a tune.

entries.clue: Solvent, take note, capitalist is bearing up! (7)

indicatorNotes.is bearing: the phrase bears, carries, the answer within its letters
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, a word going up is read from bottom to top, backwards

annotation.surface: A capitalist, financially solvent, tells everyone to take note of how well he is doing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' plays as the adjective, able to pay debts, which suits the capitalist; it is the noun, a liquid that dissolves things.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: acetone is a common solvent, the main ingredient of nail-varnish remover.

entries.clue: Robust second wine, measure of its strength? (10)

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time
hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine
proof is the scale for alcoholic strength

annotation.surface: A wine buff praises a robust second wine and wonders how strong it is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Robust' looks like a tasting note on the wine; it is the definition, meaning sturdy.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: something built to withstand knocks without damage is robust.

entries.clue: Go jump in a lake, as might frog? (3,2)

blocks.note: a rude way of telling someone to go away
what a frog does to get into the water, taken literally

annotation.surface: Telling someone to get lost, with a frog as the one who would literally jump in.
annotation.walkthrough: HOP IT is British slang for 'go away', and the frog takes the phrase literally, hopping into the lake.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom matched with an idiom: both are brusque British ways of telling someone to leave.

entries.clue: Might prove enchanting framing lovers starting out — might it? (11)

annotation.definition: Might prove enchanting framing lovers starting out — might it?

indicatorNotes.framing: a frame goes round a picture, so one word goes round the letter
indicatorNotes.starting: a word's start is its first letter, so only that is used

annotation.surface: A romantic evening for a couple setting out together, with a hopeful question at the end.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: candlelight round a couple might well prove enchanting, and the closing 'might it?' invites you to see that.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: soft candlelight surrounding a pair of new lovers is the classic enchanting setting.

entries.clue: Resolve to appear bold in a concrete jungle (11)

blocks.note: a concrete jungle is a city

annotation.surface: Someone steels themselves to look confident in a tough urban setting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' reads as a verb, to make up one's mind; it is the noun, determination.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stubborn persistence in a purpose is resolve.

entries.clue: Greenhouse gas has park warden huffy in the end (8)

indicatorNotes.in the end: only what comes at the end of the word, its final letter, is used

annotation.surface: A grumpy park warden complains about greenhouse gases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Greenhouse gas' is a set phrase, but it splits: the greenhouse is the definition and the gas is oxygen.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an orangery is a glass building for growing orange trees, a particular kind of greenhouse.

entries.clue: Day and date to eat chicken, primarily, as — this dish has it! (9)

annotation.definition: Day and date to eat chicken, primarily, as — this dish has it!

indicatorNotes.to eat: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the outer words take the others in
indicatorNotes.primarily: the primary, first, letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: to see someone = to date them

annotation.surface: A plan for a Friday date over a chicken dinner.
annotation.walkthrough: The last words turn the clue on itself: the dish described, chicken eaten on a date, is exactly what a fricassee has in it.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a fricassee is a stew of meat pieces in white sauce, very often chicken.

entries.clue: Suggested delicacy one has filled (5)

indicatorNotes.has filled: the letter fills a word the way food fills a stomach, sitting inside it

blocks.note: tact = delicacy in dealing with people

annotation.surface: A food critic reports that a recommended delicacy is one that has filled them up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delicacy' tempts as a treat to eat, and 'filled' backs that up; here it means tact.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: what is tacit is implied without being said outright, so merely suggested.

entries.clue: Roman emperor’s bronze embodying power (6)

indicatorNotes.embodying: to embody something is to take it into your body, so the word holds the other inside

blocks.note: a tan is a bronzed skin colour
the Raj = British rule in India

annotation.surface: A bronze statue of a Roman emperor that embodies imperial power.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a museum label, and bronze belongs there as a metal; it is the colour of a suntan.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Trajan ruled Rome from AD 98 to 117.

entries.clue: Cherry? Round object sustaining insect (7,4)

indicatorNotes.sustaining: to sustain is to hold up, and in a down clue the lower part holds up the upper

blocks.note: a cricket is a chirping insect

annotation.surface: A cherry described as a small round thing, with a bug on it.
annotation.walkthrough: Cricket is the bat-and-ball game played across Britain and the Commonwealth, and its commentators call the shiny new red ball the cherry.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang use from cricket: the new ball is the cherry, from its red colour.

entries.clue: Projection: all but one in football team active (5)

blocks.clueFragment: all but one in football team
blocks.note: a football team has eleven players

annotation.surface: A prediction that ten of a football side's eleven will be in action.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Projection' suggests a forecast in this sporting surface; it is a piece sticking out.
annotation.definitionFit: A woodworking term: the tenon is the tongue that projects from one timber to fit a mortise in another.

entries.clue: Laughing stock, ordinary bloke on feet to welcome king (8,4)

indicatorNotes.to welcome: to welcome someone is to let them in, so the bloke takes the king inside

annotation.surface: An ordinary man gets to his feet to greet the king and is laughed at.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stock' in the definition has nothing to do with farming or finance; a laughing stock is a person everyone mocks.
annotation.definitionFit: Two idioms for the same thing: a person or thing that is constantly and predictably mocked.

entries.clue: Cigarette lit, fire heartlessly put out (6,3)

indicatorNotes.heartlessly: a word without its heart has lost its middle, leaving only the outside letters
indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out of place are no longer in their proper order

blocks.note: put with its middle U gone

annotation.surface: A cigarette has been lit and the fire then put out carelessly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put out' looks like one phrase for extinguishing; it splits, with put losing its heart and out the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a filter tip is a cigarette with a filter at the mouth end.

entries.clue: Concept about country in South Africa regulating process (13)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the concept goes round everything else
indicatorNotes.in: the country is placed in South Africa, inside its abbreviation

blocks.note: Mali is a West African country

annotation.surface: A political idea concerning one African state inside another.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the country first goes into RSA, and that whole group then goes into the concept.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: normalisation is the process of bringing things into line with a norm, which regulates them.

entries.clue: Lighter game (7)

blocks.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge
a card game, the British name for blackjack

annotation.surface: A less serious game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, a flat barge that carries cargo to and from ships.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pontoon is a flat-bottomed boat like a lighter, and pontoon is also the card game known elsewhere as blackjack.

entries.clue: Effective narration (7)

blocks.note: as a blow or argument that hits home
as in the act of recounting a story

annotation.surface: Praise for a gripping piece of storytelling.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words sit side by side like a review's verdict, but each is a separate definition: one adjective, one noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: as an adjective it means striking and effective, as a noun the act of recounting a story.

entries.clue: Pose adopted by boy in a state? (7)

annotation.definitionNote: ALASKAN names a person; 'in a state' describes where they are

indicatorNotes.adopted by: an adopted child is taken into a family, so the word is taken inside the boy's name

blocks.note: to pose a question = to ask it

annotation.surface: A child in care strikes an attitude, clearly worked up about it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests being upset; it is one of the US states.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: someone from Alaska lives in a US state, so is quite literally in a state.

entries.clue: Huge flier off course, rare bird on course? (9,9)

blocks.note: in golf, an albatross is three under par on a hole

annotation.surface: A huge bird has strayed from its route, a rarity turning up on a golf course.
annotation.walkthrough: The two 'course's differ: a route, then a golf course, where birdie, eagle and albatross are ever-rarer scores below par.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: this seabird has the largest wingspan of any living bird.

entries.clue: Word of sympathy received by prophet, understood (8)

indicatorNotes.received by: what is received is taken in, so the prophet takes the word inside him

blocks.note: Gad is a prophet in the Old Testament
'there, there' is said to comfort someone

annotation.surface: A prophet hears a kind word and takes the point.
annotation.walkthrough: Gad is a minor figure, the prophet who advised King David; the usual crossword prophets are ELI and AMOS.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'I gathered' and 'I understood' both mean grasped from what was said.

entries.clue: Higher than the first sixteen characters? (4)

blocks.note: from the first letter of the alphabet to the sixteenth

annotation.surface: A question about the opening letters of the alphabet.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as A TO P: from A, the first letter, to P, the sixteenth.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a preposition meaning on top of, and a spelled-out range of the alphabet.

entries.clue: Drunk sizing up a pasty? (3-4)

annotation.surface: A drunk eyes up a pasty on the way home from the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half reads the slang word literally: a pasty, a British pastry with a savoury filling, is a sort of pie, and sizing it up is eyeing it.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang term, read once as intended and once literally.

entries.clue: Meat cut, a doctor and companion tucked in (4,4)

indicatorNotes.tucked in: things tucked in are pushed inside, like a shirt into trousers

annotation.surface: A butcher's cut of meat tucked into by a doctor and a friend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Meat cut' looks like the definition in one piece, especially with the answer a cut; only 'Meat' defines, and the cut belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a lamb chop is one kind of meat.

entries.clue: Principled observance declared? (5)

indicatorNotes.declared: what is declared is said out loud, so the word counts only by its sound

blocks.note: a rite is a religious observance

annotation.surface: A question about whether a publicly declared ritual is a matter of principle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Principled' is an adjective, so the answer is right in its moral sense, not a noun like an entitlement.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a right action is morally correct, as a principled one is.

entries.clue: Peg, callous sister upset youngster (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so in a down clue the word is turned bottom to top

blocks.note: a golf tee is a peg for the ball
Regan, King Lear's cruel daughter, sister of Goneril and Cordelia, reversed

annotation.surface: Peg is upset by her unfeeling sister, a sulky youngster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peg' poses as a girl's name at the start; it is a golf tee. The callous sister is Shakespeare's Regan.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a teenager, aged thirteen to nineteen, is one kind of youngster.

entries.clue: Take it in your own hands and chill out! (3,1,4)

annotation.definition2: Take it in your own hands

blocks.clueFragment: Take it in your own hands
blocks.note: to take hold of something physically
an order to calm down and pull yourself together

annotation.surface: Advice to someone in a flap: take control yourself and calm down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take it in your own hands' sounds like taking charge; read literally, it is grasping something.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally, to grasp something; as an idiom, a command to stop panicking.

entries.clue: Have the temerity to bring in European regulation where Dover is (8)

indicatorNotes.to bring in: to bring something in is to take it inside, so the outer word takes the others

blocks.note: to dare = to have the nerve

annotation.surface: A cross-Channel row about daring to impose EU rules at the port of Dover.
annotation.walkthrough: Dover wants to be the English Channel port, which fits the European rules; it is also the capital of the US state of Delaware.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by fact: Dover is Delaware's state capital.

entries.clue: Quiet moment in corporation, activists quickly dispersing (5,3)

indicatorNotes.in: the first pieces are put in the last one, inside it

blocks.note: corporation is jokey old slang for a paunch
mo = moment, as in 'half a mo'

annotation.surface: A pause at a company as protesters break up and leave.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' plays as a company but is old slang for a pot belly.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a flash mob gathers suddenly in public to perform, then melts away fast.

entries.clue: A border sign breaking three times now (2,3,6)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the pieces break into another group, splitting it apart

blocks.note: a hem is a border of cloth

annotation.surface: A sign on a border crossing is broken three times.
annotation.walkthrough: The break comes late, between the second and third T, which is why the letters are hard to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the phrase means at the present time, now.

entries.clue: Missing intro, musical group provides backing (7)

indicatorNotes.Missing intro: a song missing its intro has lost its opening, so the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a band's bass players, as a group

annotation.surface: A band without its opening number still supplies the backing music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' fits the musical surface as a backing band; it means support.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to assist is to back someone up with help.

entries.clue: Stomach after lemon chicken (11)

indicatorNotes.after: the stomach comes after, following the lemon in the answer

blocks.note: lemon is a shade of yellow

annotation.surface: A recipe: lemon chicken, something to stomach.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lemon chicken' looks like one dish; lemon is wordplay and chicken, a coward, is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: both words are informal for a coward.

entries.clue: Spillage of tear, or novice crying over spilt milk? (12)

indicatorNotes.Spillage of: spilt things scatter and land any which way, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A beginner weeps over a spilled drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the proverb 'it's no use crying over spilt milk', about fussing over something trivial and past.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: crying over spilt milk is getting upset out of proportion to a small loss.

entries.clue: Smashing up of gate amuses a pig, perhaps (7,4)

indicatorNotes.Smashing up of: something smashed up is in pieces, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A pig finds it funny to smash through a farm gate.
annotation.walkthrough: The pig is not the animal in the farmyard picture but what it ends up as.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example turned round: sausagemeat is minced pork, and a pig is one source of it.

entries.clue: Looking at wall, where ladder goes in a difficult position? (2,7,2)

annotation.definition2: Looking at wall, where ladder goes

blocks.clueFragment: Looking at wall, where ladder goes
blocks.note: a ladder leans upright on a wall, facing it
the idiom for being in trouble

annotation.surface: Someone facing a wall, with a ladder leaning on it, is in an awkward spot.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally first, a ladder propped on the wall, then as the idiom for being in trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: literally, leaning on a wall; as an idiom, facing serious difficulties.

entries.clue: Mean and ready for bare-knuckle fight? (5-6)

annotation.surface: A nasty character spoiling for a fistfight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as nasty alongside the fight; it means stingy.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the idiom for stingy, and a literal clenching of the fists.

entries.clue: Certain kennels benefit hot dog! (6,5)

indicatorNotes.kennels: to kennel a dog is to house it, so the outer word houses the others

annotation.surface: A kennels' fundraising event selling hot dogs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kennels' plays as the dogs' home; it is the verb, to house. 'Hot dog' is a snack in the surface but splits in two.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the basset hound is a short-legged, long-eared breed of dog.

entries.clue: Having experienced a close shave, tie felt different going in front (11)

indicatorNotes.different: the letters are made different by being put in another order
indicatorNotes.going in: the rearranged letters go into another word

blocks.note: a very close shave leaves you bald

annotation.surface: A man who narrowly escaped disaster now feels differently about going to the front line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A close shave' is a near miss in the surface but is taken literally, as a razor to the scalp.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: in war the front is where the fighting is, the battlefield.

entries.clue: Nub: link with heat that’s off, not on (11)

indicatorNotes.that’s off: letters that are off are out of their place, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A cooker has a heating element that's switched off, not on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off, not on' sounds like a switch; 'not on' is British for unacceptable.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: something 'not on' is out of the question, too unacceptable to consider.

entries.clue: Box opened by one with black key (5,3)

indicatorNotes.opened by: the word is opened up so others can go inside it

blocks.note: an ace counts one in cards

annotation.surface: A box is unlocked with a black key.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Box' and 'key' look like a locked box; box is the verb, to fight, and the key is on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the space bar is the long key at the bottom of a keyboard.

entries.clue: Where nation goes for oath on page, poisonous stuff (9)

blocks.note: N (nation) is placed after DAM to spell DAMN, an oath

annotation.surface: A newspaper page on where the country is heading, and the toxic content printed there.
annotation.walkthrough: An unusual device: the clue asks where N goes to make an oath, and the answer to that question supplies the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A mining term: afterdamp is the poisonous gas, mostly carbon monoxide, left after an explosion underground.

entries.clue: Perhaps ticker in particular good before brief turns (3,5)

indicatorNotes.turns: a word that turns round faces the other way, so it reads backwards

annotation.surface: A heart, perhaps, in good shape before short bouts of exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ticker' is slang for the heart; here it is something that ticks, and 'perhaps' marks the answer as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a kitchen egg timer may tick away the minutes.

entries.clue: Deck held in casino, it appearing to the left (5)

indicatorNotes.held in: the answer is held inside the words that follow
indicatorNotes.appearing to the left: in an across clue, text running to the left runs backwards

blocks.note: casinO IT APpearing, read right to left

annotation.surface: A deck of cards is held at a casino table and shown to the player on the left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deck' is a pack of cards in the casino picture; it is an outdoor platform.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a patio and a deck are both outdoor areas beside a house for sitting out.

entries.clue: Getting better marks coming in last? (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.coming in: the letter comes in, entering the phrase

blocks.note: last in line = on the end
M = marks, the old German currency

annotation.surface: A student's grades are improving though they still come in last.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Marks' suggests school grades in the surface; it is the old German currency.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone on the mend is recovering from illness or injury.

entries.clue: Pulp eaten by bird, sticky thing (8)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so the bird takes the pulp in

blocks.note: a flyer = a bird, something that flies

annotation.surface: A bird eats mushy food and ends up with something stuck to it.
annotation.walkthrough: The bird is not a species but anything that flies, a flyer.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: flypaper is coated with glue to trap flies.

entries.clue: Playwright confident in speech? (4)

indicatorNotes.in speech: in speech a word is heard, not seen, so only its sound matters

annotation.surface: A playwright who sounds very sure of himself when he talks.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone needs a southern British accent, where the R in sure is silent and it rhymes with law.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: George Bernard Shaw was the Irish playwright who wrote Pygmalion.

entries.clue: Macbeth’s life identity: a ballad too stupid? (1,4,4,2,2,5)

annotation.answer: A TALE TOLD BY AN IDIOT

indicatorNotes.stupid?: stupid letters have lost their sense, so they are jumbled up

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether a ballad about Macbeth's identity is too foolish.
annotation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Macbeth, life 'is a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing'. The indicator 'stupid' echoes the idiot of the quotation.
annotation.definitionFit: A quotation: Macbeth's 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow' speech describes life in exactly these words.

entries.clue: Cooler leader in actuality behind a web of deceit? (4,3)

indicatorNotes.a web of: threads in a web are tangled together, so the letters are tangled
indicatorNotes.leader in: the leader of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.behind: the letter goes behind, after the rest

annotation.surface: A cool leader who is in fact hiding behind a tangle of lies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' looks like a comparative adjective about the leader; it is a noun, a cold drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a cooler is a cold drink, and iced tea is a classic one.

entries.clue: Spirited opening of performance, promising (6)

indicatorNotes.opening of: as a show's opening is its very start, the word's first letter is used

annotation.surface: A theatre review of a lively, promising first night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opening' reads as an opening night; it points to the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean brave and full of spirit.

entries.clue: Incompetent type, one blowing something out of proportion, ultimately (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimate means last, so only the word's last letter is used

blocks.note: last letter of proportion, which the bugler blows into his instrument

annotation.surface: A clumsy person who blows things out of proportion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blowing something out of proportion' is an idiom for exaggerating; here it splits into a bugler and a single letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bungler does things clumsily, an incompetent sort.

entries.clue: Suit: fine one, choice clothes (5)

indicatorNotes.clothes: as clothes go round a body, the word wraps round the others

blocks.note: your best bet = your best choice

annotation.surface: A tailor's note: a good suit, one fine choice of clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suit' and 'clothes' are tailoring in the surface; suit is the verb, and clothes is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the verb sense: what befits you is appropriate to you.

entries.clue: Tender secretary at length scrubbing back (7)

indicatorNotes.scrubbing back: the back of the word is scrubbed out, removing its last letter

blocks.note: in full = at length, losing its last L

annotation.surface: A secretary spends ages scrubbing someone's back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender' sounds loving in this bath-time picture; it means sore.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a tender spot hurts when touched.

entries.clue: Part of jacket, copy reading between the lines? (5)

indicatorNotes.reading between: the copy is read between the two lines, sitting with one on each side

annotation.surface: A book jacket's blurb, and a copy of it read for hidden meaning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reading between the lines' is the idiom for spotting hidden meaning; here it places the copy inside two Ls.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by part: the lapel is the folded-back front edge of a jacket's collar.

entries.clue: Eg plane orbiting Klingon kingdom identified initially — by one of those? (7)

indicatorNotes.orbiting: a body in orbit circles round another, so the tree goes round the letters
indicatorNotes.initially: each word gives only its initial, the letter it starts with

blocks.note: first letters of Klingon Kingdom Identified

annotation.surface: A spaceship circles an alien empire, recognised straight away by a sci-fi fan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' plays as an aircraft or spacecraft; it is the tree. The definition points back: a Klingon kingdom is what a Trekkie would spot at once.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by reference: Klingons come from Star Trek, and 'one of those' is a fan of the show.

entries.clue: Rendering of a perfect theme in pastoral scene (4,9)

indicatorNotes.Rendering of: a rendering is a new version, so the letters are rendered in a new order

annotation.surface: An artist's rendering of an ideal subject in a country landscape.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about painting, and fittingly the answer names a genre of painting, as in Watteau's scenes of people at leisure outdoors.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French term: a fête champêtre is an outdoor country party, and a painting of one is a pastoral scene.

entries.clue: A bolt screwed into rod one’s pocketed! (4,5)

indicatorNotes.screwed: a thing screwed is twisted round, so the letters are twisted into a new order
indicatorNotes.into: the rearranged letters go into another word

annotation.surface: A bolt is screwed into a rod, and someone has walked off with one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pocketed' suggests stolen; the definition means fitted with pockets.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the table used for pool has six pockets for the balls.

entries.clue: Mangy spud, by the sound of it? (5)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: judged only by the sound of it, so the spelling may change

blocks.note: tattie is Scottish and Northern English for potato

annotation.surface: A scruffy-looking potato.
annotation.walkthrough: A spud is a potato, and tattie is the Scottish word for one.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: both describe something shabby and worn.

entries.clue: Standard trick nailing a rudiment of drumming (10)

blocks.note: to diddle = to cheat, trick; it is nailed on after A

annotation.surface: A standard trick for nailing the basics of drumming.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nailing' reads as mastering in the surface; here it only fixes A to the trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A drumming term: the paradiddle, sticked RLRR LRLL, is one of the standard rudiments drummers learn.

entries.clue: Strong programme cut, smoke remains? (3,3)

indicatorNotes.cut: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: f = forte, loud or strong in music
an agenda is a programme, minus its last A
